A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HEIST and provide readable methods, results, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Relocated material, including v3 Figure A5 becoming v4 Figure 4, can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original HEIST evaluations for imputation, clinical prediction, annotation, clustering, and ligand–receptor prediction, together with ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–4 and Appendix E, with existing biological analyses also presented in Section 3.1.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendices B–C retain the same graph construction, positional encodings, intra-level and cross-level message passing, decoder, and training objectives.

E1.justification: Pretraining coverage and downstream datasets, modalities, tasks, and tissue conditions are unchanged. Ligand–receptor prediction and the Braak-stage case study were already included in v3 Appendix E.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparison tables retain the same baseline rows, including the aligned and unaligned CellPLM and scGPT-spatial settings. The relocated ligand–receptor discussion retains the same comparators in Table A9.

E3.justification: Training budgets, frozen-encoder probes, decoder fine-tuning, metrics, and preprocessing are unchanged. Appendix D.2 retains the same imputation masks: 4 of 30 skin markers and 16 of 200 placenta genes.

E4.justification: The component, positional-encoding, threshold, contrastive-loss, and batch-size ablations are retained. Attention, ligand–receptor, and Braak-stage analyses already appeared in v3; moving their discussion does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the five-repeat and mean-and-standard-deviation statement, including its Charville/UPMC qualification. Uncertainty reporting practices in the tables are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains fine-tuned HEIST correlations of 0.821±0.041 for placenta and 0.807±0.020 for skin; Table A9 retains ligand–receptor AUC-ROC of 0.995±0.002.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, attention and loss equations, positional-encoding formulas, and computational-complexity expressions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or theorems are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical spatial and molecular modeling, proteomics transfer, downstream performance, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: The Braak-progression and ligand–receptor interpretations move from Appendix E without substantive revision. Appendix F retains the limitations concerning mutual-information networks, absent temporal modeling, and pretraining resource requirements.

D1.justification: v4 replaces anonymous code links with the named GitHub repository, removes the future-release promise, and adds a title-page Hugging Face link. Implementation details are unchanged; the PDFs establish these access pointers, not the contents or availability of their destinations.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against hierarchical graph models, spatial methods, and single-cell foundation models are unchanged. Bibliographic differences are line wrapping and formatting.

P1.justification: v4 updates the publication header, corrects 'Corresponding Authors,' and moves the existing Braak-stage and ligand–receptor discussions into Section 3.1 with limited sentence editing. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reflows the document through narrower text and table widths, changed margins, and widespread float relocation. v3's 2×2 Figure A5 becomes a four-panel row in main-text Figure 4, while Tables A9–A11 are grouped on the final appendix page. The underlying scientific content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added Hugging Face pointer and named GitHub links improve documented resource access, while bringing existing biological analyses into Section 3.1 improves their visibility. These are limited usability gains with unchanged scientific evidence; the smaller Braak panels are a presentation tradeoff.
